mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes scalar quantities from vector quantities?

options.A: A scalar has magnitude only, while a vector has both magnitude and direction.
options.B: A scalar has direction only, while a vector has magnitude only.
options.C: Both scalar and vector have magnitude and direction.
options.D: Neither scalar nor vector have magnitude.

mcqs.answer: A scalar has magnitude only, while a vector has both magnitude and direction.
mcqs.explanation: Scalars are described by a single number (magnitude) such as mass or temperature. Vectors require both a magnitude and a specific direction, e.g., displacement or force. Option A states this correctly; the other options either reverse the definitions or claim both have the same properties, which is false.

mcqs.question: How is a vector most commonly represented in a diagram?

options.A: As a straight line segment with an arrow at one end indicating its direction.
options.B: As a single point without any arrow.
options.C: As a curved line without an arrow.
options.D: As a numerical value written on the board.

mcqs.answer: As a straight line segment with an arrow at one end indicating its direction.
mcqs.explanation: The standard graphical representation of a vector is an arrow: the length shows magnitude and the arrowhead shows direction. Options B, C, and D do not convey direction, so they are incorrect.

mcqs.question: A displacement vector is drawn as an arrow 5 cm long making an angle of 30° above the positive x‑axis. What are its magnitude and direction?
mcqs.explanation: The length of the arrow gives the magnitude (5 units). The angle shown with respect to the positive x‑axis is 30°, measured upward, so the direction is 30° above +x. Options B, C, and D alter either magnitude or direction incorrectly.

mcqs.question: Which of the following sets contains only vector quantities?
mcqs.explanation: Displacement, velocity, and force each have magnitude and a specific direction, making them vectors. Speed, mass, temperature, distance, time, work, energy, and power are scalars. Momentum (option C) is a vector, but the other two are scalars, so the set is not “only vectors”.

mcqs.question: Which statement reflects a common misconception about vectors?

options.A: Speed, being the magnitude of velocity, is a vector quantity.
options.B: Velocity has both magnitude and direction, so it is a vector.
options.C: Force is a vector because it has magnitude and direction.
options.D: Mass is a vector because it can be added.

mcqs.answer: Speed, being the magnitude of velocity, is a vector quantity.
mcqs.explanation: The misconception is that speed, which is only the magnitude of velocity, is a vector. In reality, speed is a scalar. Options B and C correctly describe vectors, while D is an incorrect statement but not a typical student misconception about vectors.

mcqs.question: Two vectors of equal magnitude are drawn from the same point: one along the positive x‑axis and the other at 60° above the x‑axis. What is the direction of their resultant measured from the x‑axis?
mcqs.explanation: Represent each vector as components: the first is (1, 0); the second (cos 60°, sin 60°) = (0.5, 0.866). Adding gives (1.5, 0.866). The angle θ = arctan(0.866/1.5) ≈ 30°. Hence the resultant points 30° above the x‑axis. The other angles are not supported by the component calculation.

mcqs.question: Vector P has magnitude 8 units and points 20° north of east. Vector Q has magnitude 10 units and points 20° south of east. Which statement is true?

options.A: Both vectors have the same magnitude.
options.B: Vector Q has a larger magnitude than Vector P.
options.C: Vector P points in the same direction as Vector Q.
options.D: Vector P has a larger magnitude than Vector Q.

mcqs.answer: Vector Q has a larger magnitude than Vector P.
mcqs.explanation: Magnitude of P is 8 units, Q is 10 units, so Q is larger. Their directions differ (north vs. south of east), so they are not the same. Option B correctly compares magnitudes; the others are false.

mcqs.question: In a typical JEE physics problem, which of the following quantities is NOT a vector?
mcqs.explanation: Momentum, acceleration, and force each have magnitude and direction, making them vectors. Work is defined as the scalar product of force and displacement and has only magnitude, so it is a scalar. Hence option C is the correct answer.
